translationRepairs: In the second year of Long'an under Emperor An Yi (
In the second year of Long'an under Emperor An (
乙 in 安皇帝乙 is the volume sub-section marker, not part of the emperor's name.
Murong Yi, the Wei prince serving under the Northern Wei, entered Ye and took possession of its granaries.
Yi, Prince Wei (衛王) of the Northern Wei, entered Ye and took possession of its granaries.
魏衛王儀 is a Northern Wei prince, not a Murong of Yan.
Fearing trouble in the eastern provinces once he had gone, Gui re-established a mobile headquarters at Zhongshan and left Murong Yi, Prince of Wei, to hold it;
Fearing trouble in the eastern provinces once he had gone, Gui re-established a mobile headquarters at Zhongshan and left Yi, Prince Wei (衛王), to hold it;
衛王儀 is the Northern Wei prince Yi, not a Murong.
Qifu Gangui of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou against the Liang cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu. Yizhou took all three, carried off more than ten thousand people, and withdrew.
Qifu Qiangui of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou against the Liang cities of Zhiyang, Guanwu, and Yunwu. Yizhou took all three, carried off more than ten thousand people, and withdrew.
On renwu day Bao reached Yilian. Duan Subone, Song Chimei, and other senior officers, playing on the army's fear of forced service, mutinied.
On renwu day Bao reached Yilian. Duan Sugu, Song Chimei, and other senior officers, playing on the army's fear of forced service, mutinied.

Subone's men had served under Murong Long, Prince of Gaoyang. They forced Long's son Murong Chong, also Prince of Gaoyang, onto the throne and murdered Murong Zhou, Prince of Lelang; Duan Yi, Duke of Zhongmou; and a number of royal princes.

Sugu's men had served under Murong Long, Prince of Gaoyang. They forced Long's son Murong Chong, also Prince of Gaoyang, onto the throne and murdered Murong Zhou, Prince of Lelang; Duan Yi, Duke of Zhongmou; and a number of royal princes.
On guimao day Bao and Nong turned back toward the main camp to suppress Subone and his rebels.
On guiwei day Bao and Nong turned back toward the main camp to suppress Sugu and his rebels.
速骨 is romanized Sugu. Source day is 癸未 (guiwei).
Murong Lanhan of Dunqiu, a Yan Master of Writing, plotted secretly with Duan Subone and camped his force east of the eastern city wall.
Lanhan, Prince of Dunqiu, a Yan Master of Writing, plotted secretly with Duan Sugu and camped his force east of the eastern city wall.
速骨 is romanized Sugu. Source 頓丘王蘭汗 gives no Murong surname.
Barely a hundred men were Subone's true conspirators; the rest had been dragooned and would not fight.
Barely a hundred men were Sugu's true conspirators; the rest had been dragooned and would not fight.

In the third month, on jiawu day, Subone prepared to storm the city. Murong Nong of Liaoxi, styled Huanlie, feared the walls would not hold and, seduced by Lanhan, slipped out by night to join the rebels in hope of saving himself.

In the third month, on jiawu day, Sugu prepared to storm the city. Murong Nong of Liaoxi, posthumously Prince Huanlie, feared the walls would not hold and, seduced by Lanhan, slipped out by night to join the rebels in hope of saving himself.
速骨 is romanized Sugu. 桓烈王 is his posthumous title.
At dawn Subone attacked. The defenders fought back hard, and his men fell by the hundreds.
At dawn Sugu attacked. The defenders fought back hard, and his men fell by the hundreds.
Subone then paraded Nong along the wall. Nong's name for loyalty had been the city's strength; when the defenders saw him below the ramparts, their spirit broke and they scattered.
Sugu then paraded Nong along the wall. Nong's name for loyalty had been the city's strength; when the defenders saw him below the ramparts, their spirit broke and they scattered.
Subone entered the city and let his soldiers kill and loot until the streets were heaped with corpses.
Sugu entered the city and let his soldiers kill and loot until the streets were heaped with corpses.
Subone shut Nong up inside the palace hall.
Sugu shut Nong up inside the palace hall.
Ajiaoluo, a senior officer and Subone's chief strategist, thought Murong Chong of Gaoyang too young and wanted Nong on the throne instead.
Ajiaoluo, a senior officer and Sugu's chief strategist, thought Murong Chong of Gaoyang too young and wanted Nong on the throne instead.
Subone immediately executed Rang and his fellows in reprisal.
Sugu immediately executed Rang and his fellows in reprisal.
On gengzi day Lanhan struck Subone by surprise and killed him and every one of his followers.
On gengzi day Lanhan struck Sugu by surprise and killed him and every one of his followers.
Hunting on Mount Bai, Gui saw a bear with her cubs and asked Yu Liudi, the conquering-champion general, "Your name means courage — can you wrestle that animal?"
Hunting on Mount Baideng, Gui saw a bear with her cubs and asked Yu Liudi, the conquering-champion general, "You are renowned for courage — can you wrestle that animal?"
Source place is 白登山; 卿名勇健 refers to his reputation for courage, not the meaning of his name.
Tuoba Gui recalled Murong Yi to court as an adviser and left Zun, Duke of Lueyang, to hold Zhongshan in his place.
Tuoba Gui recalled Yi to court as an adviser and left Zun, Duke of Lueyang, to hold Zhongshan in his place.
Source 王儀 gives no Murong surname; this is the Northern Wei prince Yi (p003).
Lü Zuan of Taiyuan marched against Yang Gui. Guo Nen came to his rescue and drove Zuan back in defeat.
Zuan, Duke of Taiyuan of Liang marched against Yang Gui. Guo Nen came to his rescue and drove Zuan back in defeat.
Source 涼太原公纂 gives no surname.
Qifu Gangui of Western Qin made him General Who Establishes Loyalty and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
Qiangui, King of Western Qin made him General Who Establishes Loyalty and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
Source 西秦王乾歸: Qiangui, no surname given.
Lanhan agreed, recalled Di's troops, and sent Pacifying-Army General Qiu Nimuch against Qi instead.
Lanhan agreed, recalled Di's troops, and sent Pacifying-Army General Qiuni Mu against Qi instead.
Source 仇尼慕: surname Qiuni, name Mu.
On yisi day they jointly led their troops against Qiu Nimuch and routed his army.
On yisi day they jointly led their troops against Qiuni Mu and routed his army.
Source 仇尼慕: surname Qiuni, name Mu.
Terrified, Lanhan sent Crown Prince Murong Mu with an army to put them down.
Terrified, Lanhan sent Crown Prince Mu with an army to put them down.
Source 太子穆 is Lanhan's son; Murong surname is wrong.

Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhong, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen had long been close to Sheng, yet Murong Mu made them his confidants. Han and Shuang could come and go from Sheng's quarters and secretly conspired with him.

Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhong, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen had long been close to Sheng, yet Mu made them his confidants. Han and Shuang could come and go from Sheng's quarters and secretly conspired with him.
Mu (穆) is Lanhan's son; Murong surname is wrong.
On dingwei day Murong Mu defeated Di, Jianan, and their allies.
On dingwei day Mu defeated Di, Jianan, and their allies.
Mu (穆) is Lanhan's son; Murong surname is wrong.

On gengxu day, at a feast for the troops, Lanhan and Mu both drank deep. That night Sheng excused himself to the privy, climbed the wall into the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Murong Mu.

On gengxu day, at a feast for the troops, Lanhan and Mu both drank deep. That night Sheng excused himself to the privy, climbed the wall into the Eastern Palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu.
Mu (穆) is Lanhan's son; Murong surname is wrong.

Simao Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, envied Huan Xuan and did not want him to hold Jing Province. To gratify Xuan's wish, he made him Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Jiao and Guang and Governor of Guangzhou;

Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, envied Huan Xuan and did not want him to hold Jing Province. To gratify Xuan's wish, he made him Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Jiao and Guang and Governor of Guangzhou;
Wang Gong would not be swayed and memorialized the throne to campaign against Wang Yu and Simao Shangzhi and his brothers.
Wang Gong would not be swayed and memorialized the throne to campaign against Wang Yu and Sima Shangzhi and his brothers.
Simao Yuanxian, heir apparent of Kuaiji, told Daozi: "We brought on today's crisis by failing to crush Wang Gong when we had the chance.
Sima Yuanxian, heir apparent of Kuaiji, told Daozi: "We brought on today's crisis by failing to crush Wang Gong when we had the chance.

Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu, resenting Daozi's transfer of four commanderies from his jurisdiction to Wang Yu's supervision, memorialized the throne: "Jiangzhou lies in the heart of the realm, yet the western capital at Jiankang faces barbarian raiders to the north — Wang Yu ought not be given a separate command there."

Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu, resenting Daozi's transfer of four commanderies from his jurisdiction to Wang Yu's supervision, memorialized the throne: "Jiangzhou lies in the heart of the realm, yet the western garrison faces barbarian raiders to the north — Wang Yu ought not be given a separate command there."
西府 is the western garrison command, not the capital Jiankang (not named in source).

In his fury Kai sent his son Hong to Wang Gong with a warning: "The Shangzhi brothers have taken power again, and they surpass even Wang Guobao in arrogance. They mean to use the court's authority to strip the provinces of their strength and settle old scores — who knows what disaster will follow?

In his fury Kai sent his son Hong to Wang Gong with a warning: "The Shangzhi brothers have taken power again, and they wield more power than even Wang Guobao did. They mean to use the court's authority to strip the provinces of their strength and settle old scores — who knows what disaster will follow?
過於國寶 compares their power with Guobao's; 'arrogance' is not in source.

In the ninth month, on the day xinmao, Simao Daozi received the yellow battle-axe of supreme command. His heir Yuanxian was named Grand Commander for the punitive campaign. Wang Xun, Defender-in-Chief, and Xie Yan, General of the Right, were dispatched against Wang Gong; Simao Shangzhi, Prince of Qiao, against Yu Kai.

In the ninth month, on the day xinmao, Sima Daozi received the yellow battle-axe of supreme command. His heir Yuanxian was named Grand Commander for the punitive campaign. Wang Xun, Defender-in-Chief, and Xie Yan, General of the Right, were dispatched against Wang Gong; Sima Shangzhi, Prince of Qiao, against Yu Kai.
On the day jihai, Simao Shangzhi crushed Yu Kai at Niuzhu. Kai escaped alone to join Huan Xuan.
On the day jihai, Sima Shangzhi crushed Yu Kai at Niuzhu. Kai escaped alone to join Huan Xuan.

Deng Qifang of Ningshuo and Qiuchi Xian, prefect of Nanyang, marched twenty thousand men against Southern Yan and met Fa and He of that court — Central Army General and Pacifying-Army General — at Guancheng. Deng's force was routed; he fled alone on horseback.

Deng Qifang of Ningshuo and Lüqiu Xian, prefect of Nanyang, marched twenty thousand men against Southern Yan and met Fa and He of that court — Central Army General and Pacifying-Army General — at Guancheng. Deng's force was routed; he fled alone on horseback.
Source 閭丘羨: compound surname Lüqiu.
Qifu Gangui of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou, governor of Qin, along with Mu Wu, the martial guard general, and Zhai Mao, the champion general, at the head of twenty thousand cavalry against Tuyuhun.

Qiangui, King of Western Qin sent Qifu Yizhou, governor of Qin, along with Mu Wu, the martial guard general, and Zhai Mao, the champion general, at the head of twenty thousand cavalry against Tuyuhun.
Source 西秦王乾是 (乾是 a scribal variant of 乾歸); no Qifu surname given, and Gangui is a misreading.

Zhongkan heard of it and raced back south from Wuhu. He sent word to the troops at Cai Prefecture: "Unless you disband and go home at once, when I reach Jiangling I will kill every one of your families left behind."

Zhongkan heard of it and raced back south from Wuhu. He sent word to the troops at Caizhou: "Unless you disband and go home at once, when I reach Jiangling I will kill every one of your families left behind."
